text:
ashley: Heads up — saw a regression in tail latency after the kernel-picker change rolled last night. 99p jumped ~15% on streaming routes. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

mikko: saw it. digging now. quick hypothesis: flashattention swap is winning for large batches but losing on small/short-seq cases we see on streaming.

raj: do we have profiling traces that show kernel switch rates + copy times? I want to rule out paged-KV scheduling overhead too (lots of prefix-heavy traffic).

ashley: pasted a small perf excerpt from the canary run:

```
perf_summary: canary-20260301
route: /v1/stream
median_latency: 48ms
p95_latency: 120ms
p99_latency: 385ms (+15% vs baseline)
kernel_switch_ratio: 0.23
avg_batch_size: 7.2
flash_attention_time_per_token: 0.85us
native_attention_time_per_token: 0.60us
paged_kv_page_faults_per_min: 4.6
```

ashley: notes — avg_batch_size small (~7), kernel_switch_ratio non-trivial. flash time per token > native in these conditions which would explain tail.

sara: hmm that matches previous microbench: FlashAttention has better throughput for large matrices but overhead (planning/copy) kills it at small B or short S. Also paged-KV can add scheduling jitter when page faults occur.

mikko: proposed quick mitigations:
- raise continuous-batcher max_wait_ms from 8 -> 20 for streaming routes to allow slightly bigger batches.
- lower token_budget_target to bias batch formation to fewer small batches (try 256 tokens).
- add kernel-routing rule: prefer native/cuBLAS when seq_len < 128 OR batch_size < 10.
- enable paged-kv prefetching for common prefix sizes.

raj: +1. Also add a metric for per-kernel enqueued_time and device_mem_copy_time so we can validate overhead chain.

ashley: quick config snippet for the batcher (will try locally):
```
continuous_batcher:
  max_wait_ms: 20
  min_batch_size: 4
  token_budget_target: 256
  queue_policy: oldest_first
kernel_router:
  rules:
    - condition: seq_len < 128 OR batch_size < 10
      prefer: native
    - condition: else
      prefer: flash
paged_kv:
  prefetch_threshold: 512
  max_prefetch_pages: 2
```

bench-bot: perf-run #2345 finished. canary -> baseline diff: p99 +14%, avg tokens/sec -3%. Full histogram uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/2345

sara: can we avoid a hard switch? maybe do a smooth fallback — use flash but run a micro-check: if device_copy_time > X, fall back to native for the remainder of the batch. That avoids too many global policy changes.

mikko: good idea. also consider sticky kernel assignments per client session for short-lived chat streams; avoids per-request planning thrash.

raj: experiment proposal: A/B three arms for 4 hours each on low-traffic shard:
A: baseline (current picker)
B: increased max_wait_ms + token_budget_target=256
C: kernel-router rule (prefer native for short seq)
Measure: p50/p95/p99, kernel_switch_ratio, avg_batch_size, device_copy_time.

ashley: I'll schedule the A/B and create dashboards for those metrics. tagging @sara for prefetch change PR.

sara: will open PR for paged-kv prefetch with metrics. small risk: extra memory use, will gate behind rollout flag.

mikko: one more gotcha — function/tool-calling flows have many short generator tokens; ensure generator paths hit the same routing rules (they sometimes bypass batcher optimizations).

ashley: noted. thanks all. starting canary->A/B tomorrow morning. will post results here. :thumbsup:
